markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (99%)** · Confident · Careful review
Conformal set is Benign only, but the second model (MUSK) disagrees.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 99%, InSitu 1% | Strongly favors Benign |
| Conformal set | {Benign} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.99 / 92nd percentile | Not flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Different top class |
| Similar cases | 5/5 Benign | All neighbors agree |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 8) · ↓ invasive · Scarce; score below typical [F2] · Validated
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 6, 7, 8) · ↓ invasive · Prominent benign stroma [F3] · Validated
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 1, 6, 10) · ↓ invasive · Prominent tubules [F4] · Weak
- **Frequent mitotic figures** (region 9) · ↓ invasive · Low score; failed spot check (0/20) · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; not shown to reflect the classifier. Unreliable here: mitoses, necrosis, normal lobules.

## Could be wrong if
- MUSK's different top class is correct; the single-class set doesn't resolve this.
- Region 3 holds duct-confined atypia (score 1.0, weak 12/20), pointing toward InSitu.

## Check on the slide
1. **Region 3** — look for atypical cells confined within ducts.
2. **Region 8** — confirm no infiltrating stroma; it scores highest for it.
3. **Region 9** — check for mitoses and lymphocytes; the mitoses score is unreliable.
